stem: Print shop X charges a \$30 setup fee plus \$0.12 per page. Print shop Y charges \$0.20 per page with no setup fee, but it takes 25% off the total cost of any order of more than 500 pages. For which of the following numbers of pages is shop X's price less than shop Y's price?
solution: Up to 500 pages, X is cheaper when \(30 + 0.12n < 0.20n\), that is, \(30 < 0.08n\), so \(n > 375\).
Above 500 pages, shop Y charges 75% of \(0.20n\), which is \(0.15n\). X is cheaper when \(30 + 0.12n < 0.15n\), that is, \(n > 1{,}000\).
So X is cheaper for \(375 < n \le 500\) and for \(n > 1{,}000\). Of the choices, only \(1{,}200\) works: \(174 < 180\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This ignores the 25% discount. For 600 pages, X costs 102 dollars, but Y costs \(0.75(120) = 90\) dollars.
explanation.B: Correct. For \(1{,}200\) pages, X costs \(30 + 144 = 174\) dollars and Y costs \(0.75(240) = 180\) dollars.
explanation.C: Incorrect. For \(1{,}000\) pages the prices are equal, 150 dollars each, so X's price is not less than Y's.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This reverses the result \(n > 375\). For 350 pages, X costs \(30 + 42 = 72\) dollars and Y costs 70 dollars.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'B': 'A', 'D': 'B', 'C': 'C', 'A': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'B', 'B': 'D', 'C': 'C', 'D': 'A'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
X = lambda n: 30 + Rational(12, 100)*n
Y = lambda n: Rational(20, 100)*n*(Rational(3, 4) if n > 500 else 1)
ok = [k for k in choices if X(value(choices[k])) < Y(value(choices[k]))]
assert ok == [answer]
assert X(1000) == Y(1000) and X(375) == Y(375)
